title: HISTORY & TIMELINE
body:
1991        — Independence of Armenia; diplomatic relations with France
              established, laying groundwork for educational cooperation.

Nov 4, 1995 — Franco-Armenian cultural, scientific and technical cooperation
              agreement signed (Paris). Both governments formally commit to
              establishing a joint higher education institution.

Nov 23, 1998— Protocol between Armenian Ministry of Education and French
              Embassy in Armenia specifying the operational and pedagogic
              framework. Jean Moulin Lyon 3 University designated as primary
              French academic partner.

2000        — UFAR officially opens. Bachelor's degrees in Law, Management,
              Finance, and Marketing offered from the outset. Dual Armenian-
              French diploma principle adopted from day one. UFAR described as
              the "mainstay of Francophonie in Armenia."

2003        — Gains intergovernmental (interstate) university status in Armenia.
              UGAB France partnership launched: 30 students/year intern in
              France (Paris & Lyon).

2011        — Joins Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie (AUF) as a member.
              Chaire Senghor de la Francophonie established at UFAR.

2014        — Coordinates TEMPUS project "Promoting quality and recognition of
              transnational education in Armenia and Georgia."
              Coordinates Erasmus+ Cycle 3 Quality Assurance project.

Sept 2017   — New Franco-Armenian bilateral treaty (Décret n° 2017-1348, signed
              Paris March 8, 2017) reaffirms UFAR as non-profit foundation with
              equal joint administration. France funds Rector/key positions;
              Armenia provides tax and military-service concessions for UFAR.

c. 2018     — IMA Faculty of Computer Science expanded significantly.
              New building opens at 1 Paruyr Sevak Street. Bachelor's and
              Master's programs in Informatics developed with Toulouse 3 Paul
              Sabatier University.

2020–2021   — UFAR becomes first and only university in Armenia to receive
              UN PRME (Principles for Responsible Management Education)
              accreditation. Announced May 12, 2021.

July 2021   — Master's in Artificial Intelligence launched (first in Armenia
              with military deferment rights).

Jan 2023    — Zaruhi Soghomonyan appointed new Vice-Rector of UFAR.

March 2023  — Armenian government decision grants military deferment right for
              AI Master's students. AI Master's is the only program in Armenia
              with this status.

April 2023  — Galaxy Group signs MoU with UFAR.

Sept 2022   — Salwa Nacouzi appointed new Rector (first female Rector), by the
              French government. Succeeds Bertrand Venard (Lyon 3).

Oct 2022    — Salwa Nacouzi elected Vice-President of the International Network
              of Senghor Chairs of Francophonie.

Nov 2023    — WBL4JOB EU-funded project conference.

Oct 23, 2024— UFAR's joint Armenian-French accreditation presented at European
              Quality Assurance Forum (November 22, 2024). First joint
              accreditation in Armenia.

Nov 20, 2024— WBL4JOB concluding conference at UFAR (with Univ. Strasbourg,
              IMC University of Applied Sciences, Lyon 3).

April 2025  — Legal Clinic (Clinique Juridique) opens at UFAR. Law students
              provide legal aid to clients under faculty supervision. One of the
              very few such university clinics in Armenia.

June 16, 2025— "AI for Good" (ԱԲ-ն հօգուտ հանրության) workshop & hackathon
              held at UFAR.

July 19, 2025— New Master's program: "International Public and Criminal Law"
              announced.

Sept 16, 2025— UFAR's 25th anniversary graduation ceremony (promotion "Komitas
              2025") held at Yerevan Opera House. >97% employment rate for
              graduating class reported. First Alumni Gala Dinner held.

Sept 9, 2025 — UFAR announces international mobility programs 2026–2028.

Nov 20, 2025— Erasmus+ mobility scholarships competition announced.

2026         — Applications for 2026–2027 academic year open March 2, 2026
              (Bachelor's). Master's applications: Phase 1 deadline Feb 15;
              Phase 2 deadline March 31; Phase 3 deadline July 15 (if places
              available).

LEGAL & GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK
  UFAR is a non-profit foundation governed by both Armenian and French law.
  The 2017 bilateral treaty codifies its structure. The Board of Trustees
  (Հոգաբարձուների Խորհուրդ) is the supreme governing and supervisory body.

title: MISSION & UNIQUE VALUE PROPOSITION
body:
UFAR's mission is to train Armenia's future professionals with a French-style
education, strengthening Franco-Armenian academic, cultural, and professional
ties. The institution identifies four key differentiating pillars:

1. INTEGRITY
   Integrity is foundational to UFAR since its inception. The university
   enforces unbiased assessment, examination oversight, and discipline
   as core institutional practices. Students internalize integrity values
   throughout their academic careers. UFAR has implemented a Soldier-Student
   Reintegration Program and a Return-to-Success Reintegration Program.

2. PROFESSIONALIZATION
   Only 4% of graduates are currently seeking work (2025 data). UFAR
   continuously studies labor market requirements and updates curricula
   and teaching methods. The "Accelerator 28"
   entrepreneurship program supports students in launching their own
   ventures. Annual Job Fairs (18th edition held in Nov 2022).
   Professional insertion surveys published annually (2023, 2024, 2025).

3. GATEWAY TO THE WORLD
   Dual diplomas (French/European + Armenian), international faculty,
   frequent contact with foreign professors. Connections to OIF
   (Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie), AUF (Agence
   Universitaire de la Francophonie), regional Francophone bodies,
   and Erasmus+ networks. Lyon 3 referred to as UFAR's "Mother University."
   Toulouse 3 Paul Sabatier partnership since 2018.

4. EDUCATING A FEMALE ELITE
   73.6% of students are women. UFAR actively cultivates female leadership.
   Programs: "Francophone Digital Career Campus" (2020), "Women of Thought,
   Women of Action" (2021), "Leadership Women" alumni union.
   70% of Accelerator 28 entrepreneurs are women.

title: FACULTIES & ACADEMIC STRUCTURE
body:
UFAR currently operates FIVE FACULTIES offering Bachelor's and Master's degrees,
plus PhD programs in three disciplines.

Academic framework: Bologna Process — Bachelor's = 8 semesters / 240 ECTS;
Master's = 4 semesters / 120 ECTS. All programs lead to DUAL STATE DIPLOMAS
(one Armenian from UFAR, one French from partner university).

FACULTY 1: LAW (Iravagitutyun / Droit)
  Level:         Bachelor's + Master's + PhD
  French Partner: Jean Moulin Lyon 3 University
  Campus:        Main Campus, 10 Davit Ankhaght St.
  Bachelor's Curriculum:
    - 8 semesters, 240 ECTS
    - 6 semesters toward French Law degree (Lyon 3)
    - Armenian public & private law, international law (yrs 1-2)
    - French law introduced from Year 3
    - Strong focus on legal research methodology and oral defense
    - Mandatory 7-week internship (end of bachelor's cycle)
    - Internship location: Armenia or abroad (law firm, public org, etc.)
  Entrance Exams: Social Studies (Hasarakagitut'yun) + Armenian Language
  Career Paths: Lawyer/Avocat, Notary, Judge (after competitions),
    Legal Advisor (banks/NGOs/insurance/intl orgs), National Security Services,
    Legal Research & Teaching
  Master's — International, Private & Comparative Law; International
    Public & Criminal Law (NEW 2025/2026 program):
    - 4 semesters, 120 ECTS
    - Languages: Armenian, French, English
    - Year 1: 14-week internship
    - Year 2: 6-month mandatory internship + final thesis with individual
      supervisor (oral defense in French)
    - Group size in TD sessions: max 40 students
  PhD: Available in Law

FACULTY 2: MANAGEMENT (Karavaryum / Gestion)
  Level:         Bachelor's + Master's + PhD
  French Partner: Jean Moulin Lyon 3 University
  Campus:        Main Campus
  Bachelor's Curriculum:
    - 8 semesters, 240 ECTS
    - 6 semesters toward French Management degree (Lyon 3)
    - In-depth theoretical knowledge in management and economics
    - Prepares economists, managers, and financial executives
    - Mandatory 7-week internship (end of bachelor's cycle)
  Entrance Exams: Mathematics + Foreign Language (French/English/German)
    OR Armenian Language
  Career Paths: Economist, Financial Manager, Banking & Insurance Specialist,
    Financial Analyst, Financial Advisor
  Master's — Management, Finance & Control:
    - 4 semesters, 120 ECTS; Languages: Armenian & French
    - Deep theoretical knowledge in economics, management, finance
    - Year 1: 3-month internship + evaluative summary report
    - Year 2: 6-month internship + final thesis defense

FACULTY 3: MARKETING & DIGITAL BUSINESS (Marketing / Marketing et Commerce)
  Level:         Bachelor's + Master's + PhD
  French Partner: Jean Moulin Lyon 3 University
  Campus:        Main Campus
  Bachelor's Curriculum:
    - 8 semesters, 240 ECTS
    - 6 semesters toward French Marketing & Digital Business degree (Lyon 3)
    - Combines theory and practice in marketing, sales, decision-making
    - Representatives of leading companies participate in teaching
    - Mandatory 7-week internship (internship report required)
    - Digital marketing projects required
  Career Paths: Organization/Company Manager, Commercial Director,
    Marketing/Sales Director, Advertising Agency Director, International Trade
    Manager, PR Manager, Brand Manager, Project Manager, Merchandiser,
    Business Analyst
  Master's — Marketing & Sales:
    - 4 semesters, 120 ECTS; Languages: Armenian & French
    - Strong emphasis on marketing, sales, communication, company collaboration
    - Year 1: 3-month internship
    - Year 2: 6-month internship (Armenia or abroad) + final thesis
  PhD: Available in Marketing

FACULTY 4: FINANCE (Finansner / Finance)
  Level:         Bachelor's only (Master's under Management faculty)
  French Partner: Jean Moulin Lyon 3 University
  Campus:        Main Campus
  Bachelor's Curriculum:
    - 8 semesters, 240 ECTS; Full-time
    - Extended internship structure in final year: 26 weeks total
      (7 weeks full-time + remainder part-time)
    - Internship report evaluated
  Language of Instruction:
    - Years 1-2: Armenian
    - Years 3-4: Armenian & French
  Career Paths: Financial Manager, Accountant, Auditor, Financial Analyst,
    Statistician-Economist Analyst

FACULTY 5: COMPUTER SCIENCE & APPLIED MATHEMATICS — IMA
  (Informatika / Informatique et Mathématiques Appliquées)
  Level:         Bachelor's + Master's
  French Partner: Toulouse 3 Paul Sabatier University (partnership since 2018)
  Campus:        IMA Campus, 1 Paruyr Sevak St.
  Bachelor's Curriculum (IMA):
    - 8 semesters, 240 ECTS; In-person
    - 6 semesters toward French Computer Science degree
    - Strong practical component: one-third of all coursework is practical
    - Programming, systems, networks, databases, computer architecture
    - Mandatory 7-week internship (end of bachelor's cycle)
    - Written internship report for evaluation
  Language Progression (IMA Bachelor's):
    - Year 1: Armenian
    - Year 2: English
    - Years 3 & 4: French & English
  Career Paths: Application Developer, Programmer, Project Manager,
    Information Security Officer, Database Administrator, Network Administrator
  Master's — Computer Science / Artificial Intelligence Systems:
    - 4 semesters, 120 ECTS
    - Dual diploma: UFAR (Armenian) "Artificial Intelligence Systems" +
      Toulouse 3 Paul Sabatier (French) "Artificial Intelligence:
      Foundations and Applications"
    - INSTRUCTION LANGUAGE: English (and French)
    - The ONLY AI Master's program in Armenia granting military deferment
      (Armenian Government Decision — see e-gov.am/gov-decrees/item/40045/)
    - Open to both UFAR graduates AND external applicants
    - AI domains covered: digital image processing, computer graphics, NLP,
      information retrieval, robotics, e-commerce
    - Year 1 opportunities: 2-month internship, supervised university project,
      small group work (S8), small group research (S8), group "Masterpiece"
      project (S9–S10)
    - Year 2: minimum 5-month internship in lab or company (Armenia or abroad)
    - Career fields: Aviation & Space, Healthcare AI, Agricultural Technology,
      Informatics, Automated Systems, Scientific Research, Smart Cities,
      Industry 4.0, Robotics, Computer Graphics

POSTGRADUATE / PhD:
  PhD programs available in:
    - Law (Iravagitut'yun)
    - Marketing
    - Management (Economics of the Economy and its Sectors)
    - Informatics & Applied Mathematics (PhD scholarship offered)

title: LANGUAGE OF INSTRUCTION
body:
French proficiency is NOT required at admission.

UFAR provides structured intensive French language training during the first
two years. Approximately 90% of students who enter without French achieve
certified B2 level (CEFR) by the time they begin their 3rd year.

Continuation beyond Year 2 is conditional on passing the standardized
French language test (internationally recognized, CEFR framework).

At least 20% of undergraduate courses (from Year 3) are in French.
Approximately 50% of graduate-level (Master's) courses are in French.
Thanks to visiting professors from Lyon 3 and Toulouse 3.

Thesis/capstone projects are submitted and orally defended in French.

LANGUAGE PROGRESSION — BACHELOR'S (General: Law, Management, Marketing):
  Year 1: Armenian + intensive French
  Year 2: Armenian + intensive French (continued)
  Year 3: Armenian & French (≥20% French)
  Year 4: French, Armenian, and English

LANGUAGE PROGRESSION — BACHELOR'S FINANCE:
  Years 1-2: Armenian
  Years 3-4: Armenian & French

LANGUAGE PROGRESSION — IMA BACHELOR'S (Computer Science):
  Year 1: Armenian
  Year 2: English
  Years 3-4: French & English

LANGUAGE PROGRESSION — MASTER'S (AI):
  All years: English (and French for dual-diploma requirements)

Estimated French instruction: ~9,000+ hours of French taught per year across
all programs.

ACCEPTED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATES for simplified admission (without foreign
language exam):
  French: DELF B1 or DELF Junior B1
  English: IELTS Academic, TOEFL (new scale: min 3.4/6 per section, 3.5/6
           overall as of Jan 21, 2026), Cambridge FCE/BEC Vantage/BEC Higher/
           CAE/CPE
  German: Goethe-Zertifikat B1, TELC Deutsch B1, DSD1 B1, DSD1 PRO B1,
           Test DaF (TDN4)
  Note: IELTS and TOEFL certificates valid for 2 years from date of issue.

SAT SCORE EQUIVALENCIES (2026–2027):
  IMA (Computer Science): SAT Math 650–800 → 65–80/120 on admission exam
    (multiply by 0.1 coefficient)
  Management/Finance/Marketing: SAT Math 630–800 → 56.7–72/100 on admission
    exam (multiply by 0.09 coefficient)
  SAT certificate valid for max 2 years.

title: WHAT MAKES UFAR UNIQUE — SUMMARY
body:
1. The ONLY university in Armenia offering Franco-Armenian DUAL STATE DIPLOMAS
   (both an Armenian UFAR diploma and a French university diploma, recognized
   by the French Ministry of Higher Education and valid in the EU).

2. The ONLY AI Master's program in Armenia with military service deferment
   rights (by Armenian Government Decision).

3. The FIRST AND ONLY university in Armenia with UN PRME (Principles for
   Responsible Management Education) accreditation.

4. The ONLY institution in Armenia where both the Rector and Secretary General
   are required by its founding statutes to be French nationals (appointed by
   the French government).

5. One of very few Armenian universities with an on-site LEGAL CLINIC where
   students provide real legal aid under supervision.

6. 73.6–78% female student body — one of the highest female representation
   rates in the Armenian higher education sector.

7. ~9,000 hours of French language instruction per year; ~90% of students
   enter without French and achieve B2 level within 2 years.

8. Dual legal framework: Armenian law for Armenian diplomas, French law for
   French diplomas.

9. 25+ years of Franco-Armenian educational partnership with 3,600+ alumni.

10. Member of AUF (Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie) since 2011.

11. Host of the Chaire Senghor de la Francophonie since 2011.

  Full names:

    - English:  STUDENT COUNCIL OF THE FUAF
    - French:   CONSEIL DES ÉTUDIANTS DE L'UFAR
  Abbreviated:
    - Armenian: ՀՖՀՀ-ՈԽ
    - English:  SCFUAF
    - French:   CEFUFAR

ARTICLE 2 — OBJECTIVES, MISSIONS AND COMPETENCES

Art. 2.1 — General Objectives:
  1. Ensure active student participation in University governance bodies
  2. Guarantee defense of students' legitimate rights and interests
  3. Coordinate student initiatives and activities
  4. Foster personal development, autonomy, and social engagement

Art. 2.2 — Specific Missions:
  1. Establish a clear, functional organizational structure
  2. Define activity domains consistent with its student representation mission
  3. Ensure representativeness and inclusion of the entire student community
  4. Be constituted democratically by free elections, with minimum 40%
     participation per faculty and per year; electronic voting allowed
  5. Report on activities to students through regular assemblies and platforms
  6. Guarantee institutional continuity through documentation and transmission
  7. Implement decisions adopted by the student community
  8. Participate constructively in University collegial organ proceedings
  9. Ensure transparent information circulation to students
  10. Represent and defend student interests before University executive organs
  11. Develop partnerships with other student councils/associations in Armenia
      and abroad
  12. Organize academic, social, cultural, and sports activities

Art. 2.3 — Competences:
  The Council is authorized to:
  1. Prepare budget proposals for University approval/financing
  2. Propose and implement student rights protection measures
  3. Use University communication channels (including a dedicated website)
     to inform students and promote student life
  4. Create and coordinate clubs and sports activities
  5. Represent students in the University Council, Scientific and Pedagogical
     Council (CSP), and other University consultative bodies
  6. Issue (in coordination with the Communications Department) participation
     certificates, recognition certificates, and honor diplomas

ARTICLE 3 — STRUCTURE AND FUNCTIONING

Art. 3.1 — Composition and Mandate:
  - Elected by universal direct suffrage, secret ballot
  - Process determined by University administration
  - 2-year mandate
  - May be partially renewed in case of resignation, exclusion, or end of
    mandate of certain members
  - Composition: 2 representatives per faculty per year of study
    (for both Licence/Bachelor's and Master's cycles)

Art. 3.2 — Organization of Elections:
  - Elections held no later than 2 months after the start of the academic year
  - Any regularly enrolled student may stand for election by submitting
    candidacy electronically to the Direction des études (Academic Office)
  - Candidacy dossier must contain:
    a) Name, first name, and patronymic (if applicable)
    b) Year of study and faculty
    c) Object of candidacy
    d) Programme or project of the candidate
  - Each candidate presents their programme publicly before the vote
  - Candidacies must be submitted at least 7 days before the election date
  - The Academic Director (Directrice des études), on proposal from the
    outgoing Council, sets the election date and informs students by
    official email

Art. 3.3 — Voting Procedures:
  In-person vote (norm):
    - Secret ballot deposited in designated ballot box
    - Ballot lists candidates' names, faculties, and years of study
    - Voters must present student card, sign electoral register, maintain
      confidentiality
    - Ballots with multiple marks, distinctive signs, or material alterations
      are declared null
  Electronic vote (only allowed in force majeure, on decision of Academic
  Office):
    - Organized on the University's Moodle platform
    - Academic Office informs students of voting procedures at least 24 hours
      before the vote opens
    - Voting period: 09:00–20:00
  Results published on institutional platform within 2 working days of
  vote closure.
  Voting method (in-person, distance, or hybrid) determined each year by
  Academic Office decision.
  Penalty: Any candidate found guilty of electoral fraud cannot re-stand for
  4 years.

ARTICLE 4 — GOVERNING BODIES

Art. 4.1 — Internal Structure:
  a) General Assembly of the Council (AG)
  b) President
  c) Maximum 2 Vice-Presidents
  d) Secretary
  e) Permanent Commissions + ad hoc Commissions as needed

Art. 4.2 — Election of the President:
  - Election held in General Assembly session convened within 5 working days
    of election results publication
  - 2-year mandate, renewable once (1 time)
  - Eligible: students in Year 3 or 4 of Licence, or Year 1 or 2 of Master's
  - Candidacies submitted at least 3 days before the vote
  - Each candidate has 10–15 minutes to present programme
  - Count conducted by Academic Office and a Rectorat representative, in
    presence of Council members
  - If no absolute majority or tie: run-off between 2 top candidates; elected
    by simple majority

Art. 4.3 — Vice-Presidents and Secretary:
  - Elected by General Assembly on President's proposal
  - Secretary: prepares agenda, drafts minutes, follows up administratively

ARTICLE 5 — GENERAL ASSEMBLY

Art. 5.1 — Convening and Frequency:
  - Meets at least 5 times per semester, alternating between UFAR building
    and IIAP building
  - Extraordinary sessions can be convened by President or on request of
    at least 2/3 of Council members

Art. 5.2 — Powers:
  a) Proposes amendments to this Regulation → submits to CSP for validation
  b) Approves annual activity programme
  c) Defines strategic priorities for student life
  d) Elects President and Commission presidents
  e) Reviews activity reports
  f) Adopts decisions on Council reorganization
  g) Presents annual report to student body and to the Direction
  h) Designates student delegates to the CSP

Art. 5.3 — Quorum and Decision-Making:
  - Can deliberate if quorum reached: 50% + 1
  - Decisions by simple majority, unless 2/3 qualified majority required

ARTICLE 6 — PERMANENT COMMISSIONS AND WORKING GROUPS

Art. 6.1 — Commissions Created:
  a) Internal and External Communications Commission:
     Maintains relations with higher education institutions and national/
     international education structures; ensures internal student communication
  b) Educational Commission:
     Participates in academic life; formulates proposals on programmes and
     teaching conditions
  c) Marketing Commission:
     Develops Council visibility strategy; manages digital communication and
     social media in conformity with University internal regulations
  d) Resources and Activities Commission:
     Implements approved projects; organizes cultural and sports activities;
     promotes student participation in university competitions
  e) Cultural Commission:
     Plans and implements intra- and extra-university cultural events
  Ad hoc commissions or working groups may be created as needed.

Art. 6.2 — Functioning:
  - Commissions meet at least once per month
  - Draft minutes of each meeting; submit annual activity report to Council
  - Members per Commission cannot exceed 1/5 of total Council membership

ARTICLE 7 — MEMBERS' RIGHTS, DUTIES, AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Art. 7.1 — Rights:
  1. Elect and be elected to governing bodies
  2. Participate in Council management
  3. Propose initiatives and freely express opinions
  4. Receive response to any proposal or complaint within 14 working days
  5. Obligated to be members of at least 1 Commission

Art. 7.2 — Duties and Responsibilities:
  1. Respect this Regulation
  2. Actively participate in meetings
  3. Contribute to implementation of Council objectives
  4. Respect democratically adopted decisions
  5. Comply with duty of confidentiality and loyalty
  6. Communicate transparently on activities and decisions

Art. 7.3 — Early End of Mandate:
  Mandate may end in case of:
  a) 3 unjustified absences per semester (2 for Commissions)
  b) Loss of student status
  c) Deregistration, exclusion, or suspension of studies
  d) Voluntary resignation
  NOTE: Absences are considered justified in case of force majeure, illness,
  examinations, family events, or official university activities.

ARTICLE 8 — FINANCIAL PROVISIONS

Art. 8.1 — Material and Financial Resources:
  - The Council benefits free of charge from premises and equipment provided
    by the University
  - PROHIBITED: soliciting funds from sources other than those provided by the
    University for financing student association activities

Art. 8.2 — Budget Management:
  - The Council President submits the annual budget proposal to the
    Administrative and Financial Director before September 15, for Rector
    validation
  - Expenditures executed per Council decisions and controlled by Financial
    Direction
  - Annual accounts audit by Administrative and Financial Director

ARTICLE 9 — FINAL PROVISIONS

Art. 9.1 — Entry into Force:
  After approval by Scientific and Pedagogical Council (CSP) and validation
  by Board of Administration (CA). [Validated by CA: January 21, 2026]

Art. 9.2 — Revision and Dissolution:
  - Any modification follows same approval procedure (CSP + CA)
  - Council may be dissolved by motivated decision of the University Rector,
    per Armenian legislation and Foundation statutes

title: RÈGLEMENT RELATIF À L'ACCOMPAGNEMENT DES ÉTUDIANTS À BESOINS
body:
ÉDUCATIFS PARTICULIERS
     REGULATION ON SUPPORT FOR STUDENTS WITH SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS
     (Validated by CA — January 21, 2026)
     Applies to all study cycles at UFAR.

ARTICLE 1 — PURPOSE AND GENERAL PRINCIPLES:
  This regulation defines measures put in place by UFAR to ensure equal
  opportunities and inclusion for students with special educational needs
  arising from a specific learning disorder, a recognized disability, or
  a lasting medical condition. The measures guarantee that all students
  can follow their training and sit evaluations under equitable conditions,
  without lowering academic standards.

ARTICLE 2 — SCOPE OF APPLICATION:
  Students covered include those with:
  - Specific language and learning disorders (dyslexia, dysorthography,
    dyscalculia, dysgraphia, dyspraxia)
  - Attention deficit disorder with or without hyperactivity (ADHD / TDA/H)
  - Autism spectrum disorders (ASD / TSA)
  - Sensory disorders (auditory, visual, etc.)
  - Motor or neuromotor disorders
  - Psychological, psychiatric, or anxiety disorders affecting schooling
  - Any other recognized medical condition requiring pedagogical or
    evaluation adaptation

ARTICLE 3 — PROCEDURE AND RECOGNITION OF STATUS:
  1. The student concerned must report their situation at the start of the
     academic year (or at the time the disorder manifests) to the Vice-
     Rector in charge of student life OR to the University Medical Service.
  2. The student presents a recent medical certificate (less than 1 year
     old) issued by a specialist doctor, speech therapist, approved
     psychologist, or recognized diagnostic centre.
  3. Based on this document, an Individualized Accommodation Plan (PAI —
     Plan d'Aménagement Individualisé) is developed jointly by:
     - The Vice-Rector in charge of student life
     - The Academic Office (Direction des études)
     - If applicable: the University doctor or an inclusion coordinator
  4. The plan specifies the nature, duration, and implementation terms
     of the accommodations granted.

ARTICLE 4 — TYPES OF ACCOMMODATION MEASURES:

4.1 — Examination and Evaluation Accommodations:
  - Extra time (generally +25% of initial time)
  - Separate or quiet exam room, limited number of candidates
  - Reading instructions aloud or clarification of written instructions
  - Use of a computer with spell-checker enabled (if justified)
  - Secretarial/scribing assistance for transcribing answers

4.2 — Pedagogical Accommodations:
  - Enlarged or adapted font (Arial, OpenDyslexic, etc.)
  - Specific color printing for students with visual or concentration
    disorders
  - Authorized medical break(s) during long exams
  - Priority access to course materials and digital documents
  - Provision of academic materials in electronic form before classes
  - Authorization to record lectures (after professor's approval)
  - Accompaniment by a pedagogical tutor or peer-student referent
  - Adaptation of homework/assignment deadlines
  - Tolerance in grading spelling or expression errors for diagnosed
    dys-disorders, when linguistic quality is not the primary evaluation
    objective

ARTICLE 5 — CONFIDENTIALITY AND PRIVACY:
  1. Medical or personal information communicated within the framework of
     this system is strictly confidential.
  2. Can only be transmitted to persons directly involved in implementing
     the accommodations (teachers, exam officers, relevant administrative
     services).
  3. The student may at any time request modification or suspension of
     their accommodations.

ARTICLE 6 — DURATION AND RE-EVALUATION:
  1. The accommodation plan is valid for one academic year and must be
     renewed each year with an updated supporting document.
  2. In case of evolution of the medical situation, a re-evaluation may
     be requested by the student or the University.

ARTICLE 7 — RESPONSIBILITIES AND FOLLOW-UP:
  1. Vice-Rector in charge of student life is responsible for
     administrative follow-up, implementation, and coordination.
  2. Academic Office ensures consistent application of the regulation
     and sensitization of teachers to student needs.
  3. Teachers are invited to foster an inclusive climate, collaborate with
     relevant services, and show kindness within pedagogical objectives.
  4. An annual evaluation report on the system may be presented to the CSP.

ARTICLE 8 — FINAL PROVISIONS:
  1. Enters into force from CSP adoption, applies to all study cycles.
  2. Situations not covered by this text examined by Academic Office in
     consultation with Vice-Rector and Medical Service.
  3. Regulation may be revised in light of evolving national standards and
     international best practices on inclusion of students with disabilities.

title: SYSTÈME DE BONIFICATION — BONUS POINTS SYSTEM
body:
(Enters into force from the academic year following adoption by
     Rector's order; validated by CA January 21, 2026)

ARTICLE 1 — PURPOSE:
  This regulation defines conditions for awarding bonus points (bonification)
  to students who have participated in extra-academic activities organized or
  recognized by the University, such as conferences, seminars, workshops,
  competitions, scientific or associative events that contribute to their
  personal and professional development. The system aims to recognize student
  engagement while respecting academic fairness.

ARTICLE 2 — NATURE AND SCOPE:
  1. Bonus points are an exceptional complement awarded to students active
     in university or scientific life.
  2. Bonification can improve the annual average grade, and may also impact
     the final ranking for the diploma mention (honors designation).
  3. Bonification CANNOT modify the calculation of excellence scholarships
     or study grants.
  4. Bonification MAY be taken into account during selection for internships
     in France or other international programs.

ARTICLE 3 — ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONS:
  1. Activities must be:
     - Related to the University's educational mission
     - Pre-approved by the Academic Office, Student Life Service, or the
       competent organizing unit
  2. Students must provide:
     - A participation certificate or official certificate
     - A brief reflective report or summary, validated by the relevant Dean,
       academic, or administrative responsible
  3. For each activity, the University will clearly communicate in the
     announcement whether or not it confers bonification rights. This info
     will appear in all communications (posters, emails, website, social
     media, etc.) to guarantee transparency and equal access.
  4. MAXIMUM LIMIT: Total bonus points awarded in a single academic year
     CANNOT EXCEED 0.5 points.

ARTICLE 4 — APPLICATION OF BONIFICATION:
  1. Bonus points are added ONLY to the annual general average.
  2. The bonification system has NO retroactive effect and applies ONLY to
     the current academic year.

ARTICLE 5 — ENTRY INTO FORCE:
  Enters into force from the academic year following adoption by the
  Rector's order. Subsequent modifications must be approved by the
  competent University bodies.

title: ORDRE N-149 — DEROGATION FOR BUSINESS PLAN COURSE FINAL GRADE
body:
(Academic Year 2024-2025)
       Signed by Rectrice Salwa Nacouzi, March 14, 2025

BACKGROUND:
  UFAR's 2024-2025 Study and Examination Regulations (paragraph D) stipulate
  that "the percentage of TD (tutorial) evaluation cannot exceed 25% of the
  overall grade for the teaching unit" when the unit consists of both lecture
  (CM) and tutorial (TD).

  The "Business Plan" (Plan d'affaires) teaching unit, shared by the
  Management and Marketing faculties for Licence 3 level (equivalent to
  Year 4 of Bachelor's), consists of:
    - 16.5 hours of lecture (CM) — taught by a visiting French professor
    - 15 hours of tutorial (TD) — under responsibility of two TD instructors,
      structured as a year-long project with 4 oral presentations
      (soutenances) by mixed groups of students from both faculties

DEROGATION (for 2024-2025 only):
  Considering the number of TD hours relative to CM hours, and the common
  evaluation methods across both faculties, the final grade for the
  "Business Plan" teaching unit shall be composed of:
    - 40%: average of TD grades
    - 60%: final written exam (corresponding to CM)

  This derogates from the standard study and examination regulations which
  would otherwise limit TD weight to 25%.

ENTRY INTO FORCE: March 14, 2025 (for academic year 2024-2025)

title: ORDRE N-292 — MAXIMUM PRINCIPLE FOR TUITION REDUCTIONS,
body:
COMPENSATIONS, AND ALLOWANCES (June 13, 2024)
       Signed by Rectrice Sandra Nacouzi Bourdichon
       Legal basis: RA Law on Foundations (Art. 27.3.3 & 27.3.8),
                    RA Law on Higher and Postgraduate Professional Education
                    (Art. 6.4.2.2), UFAR Statutes (Art. 6.14.3 & 6.14.7)

RULE 1 — STATE AID SUPERSEDES UNIVERSITY PRE-APPROVED AID:
  If a reduction, compensation, or allowance granted to a student by the
  University through the pre-approval procedure is smaller in amount than
  that approved by the Republic of Armenia for annual tuition fees, then
  upon the State's approval of such aid, the University's pre-approval order
  (or the relevant part thereof) may be invalidated.

RULE 2 — ACADEMIC REDUCTIONS (EXCEPTION):
  The above rule does NOT apply to pre-approved academic reductions.
  However, if the sum of the State-granted reduction and the University's
  pre-approved academic reduction exceeds 100% of the annual tuition fees,
  the amount of the University's pre-approved academic reduction may be
  reduced by the percentage exceeding 100%.

RULE 3 — IMPLEMENTATION COMMISSION:
  A Commission is established by Rector's order to implement Rules 1 and 2.
  Composition:
    - Rector of the University (Chair, casting vote in case of tie)
    - Vice-Rector for Education, Research, and University Life
    - Administrative and Financial Director
    - Director of Academic Affairs (Directeur des études)
  Quorum: 3 out of 4 members present and participating.
  Decisions: Simple majority, open vote.

ENTRY INTO FORCE: June 13, 2024 (date of signature)
APPLIES TO: Legal relations arising after September 1, 2023

title: IMA-SPECIFIC ATTENDANCE RULES — TOULOUSE III REFERENCE

rules are governed not only by UFAR's internal regulations but also by the
Study and Examination Regulations of Toulouse III Paul Sabatier University

scholarship loss, 50 absences triggers possible exclusion), but the legal

attendance rules are based on Lyon 3 University regulations (via UFAR's
internal regulations derived from the Lyon 3 partnership).

to comply results in an absence being recorded.

title: IMA-SPECIFIC STUDY & EXAMINATION REGULATIONS (2025-2026)
body:
Partnership with Toulouse 3 Paul Sabatier University
    Source: Régime des études et examens de l'UFAR — Faculté d'informatique
           et de mathématiques appliquées (validated by UFAR Board of Trustees,
           July 30, 2025; effective from 2025-2026 academic year)

This regulation applies to all IMA faculty students enrolled in double
diploma programs with Toulouse 3 (Bachelor's in Computer Science, Master's
in AI). It replaces the 2024-2025 version.

A. LANGUAGE PROGRESSION (already in master file, but confirmed here):
   Bachelor's:
     Year 1 (Licence A): Armenian
     Year 2 (Licence 1): English
     Years 3 & 4 (Licence 2 & 3): French and English
   Master's: English

B. LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS FOR PROGRESSION (NEW DETAILS):
   - From Licence A to Licence 1: must validate B1 level in English
     (internal UFAR exam)
   - From Licence 1 to Licence 2: must validate B1 level in French
     (internal UFAR exam) + B2 level in English (Cambridge FCE, IELTS,
     or TOEFL). UFAR covers FCE exam fee for first attempt within UFAR's
     defined deadlines.
   - From Licence 2 to Licence 3: must obtain DELF B2 diploma (minimum
     50/100) from an accredited center in Armenia or abroad.
   - Conditional progression (AJAC): If a student passes the academic year
     but fails the required language exam (French B1, English FCE, or DELF B2),
     they are "ajourné mais autorisé à continuer" (AJAC) — enrolled in both
     the current year and the next year simultaneously. If still not obtained
     by year end, they must repeat both years.

C. INTERNSHIP DURATIONS (IMA ONLY):
   - Licence 3 (Year 4 of Bachelor's): 2 months mandatory internship
     (Note: This differs from the 7 weeks stated elsewhere in this file for
     other faculties. IMA uses 2 months.)
   - Master 1: 2 months mandatory internship
   - Master 2: 5 months mandatory internship

D. PROFESSIONAL PROJECTS (Bachelor's IMA):
   Students must complete seven (7) industry-related professional projects
   throughout their Bachelor's studies. These are evaluated as part of the
   degree.

E. ATTENDANCE RULES (IMA-specific details beyond general UFAR policy):
   - 75% attendance required for each teaching unit (CM, TD, and/or TP) to be
     authorized to sit the exam.
   - Absence requests must be submitted to the Academic Office (scolarité)
     at least one week before the first day of absence.
   - Justification for absences must be provided within 2 days of the first
     absence (notification to Director of Studies) and supporting document
     must reach the Academic Office within 8 days. Otherwise, absence is
     considered unexcused.
   - For online courses: cameras must be turned on; otherwise attendance
     is not counted.

F. EVALUATION RULES (IMA-specific):
   - Each teaching unit (UE) is assessed by at least one grade (written or
     oral, individual or collective).
   - For units consisting of CM + TD + TP: TD and/or TP evaluation weight
     cannot exceed 25% of the overall grade, EXCEPT for language courses
     (which are taught only as TD, and may have higher weight by proposal
     of chair holder and dean).
   - For 1st and 2nd year students (Licence A, Licence 1, Master 1):
     Two evaluations per semester (E1 and E2).
     - E1 occurs after approximately 50% of course hours, no later than
       week 8 of the semester.
     - E2 covers material from E1 to end of semester.
     - Make-up sessions for E1 (November) and E2 (December-January) are
       available ONLY for force majeure (e.g., hospitalization).

G. VALIDATION AND COMPENSATION (IMA-specific):
   For 1st and 2nd year students (Licence A, Licence 1, Master 1):
     - Validation is by module (not by semester). A module is passed with
       an average of at least 10/20.
     - No compensation between modules in the same semester, and no annual
       compensation between semesters.

   For 3rd and 4th year students (Licence 2, Licence 3, Master 2):
     - Semester validation: automatic if weighted average >= 10/20, even if
       individual units are below 10.
     - Annual compensation (non-automatic) between two semesters of the same
       year may be granted by the jury.
     - For Master's: Professionalization units (internships, projects >=6 ECTS,
       or choice units) are NOT compensable. Semester compensation applies
       automatically only if both conditions met: average >=10/20 AND no
       individual grade below 6/20.

H. REDOUBLEMENT (Course Repetition):
   - A student with any unvalidated semester cannot proceed to the next year.
   - When repeating a year, the student automatically keeps all grades >=10/20
     and their ECTS credits.
   - French and English course attendance is mandatory when repeating.
   - The student does NOT need to retake French/English exams if they already
     achieved >=10/20 and met the required level (B1 English in Licence A,
     B2 English in Licence 1, French B1 in Licence 1, DELF B2 in Licence 2).

I. JURY COMPOSITION (IMA-specific):
   Voting members: Rector, Director of Studies, Vice-Rector, Dean and
     Associate Dean of the faculty (or their representatives), Chair of
     Mathematics, teachers proposed by the partner university president.
   Advisory members: Teachers proposed by Dean and Associate Dean,
     Head of Academic Office, Chair of French.
   Presidency:
     - Licence A, Licence 1, Licence 2, Master 1: Rector or designee
     - Licence 3, Master 2: Dean of partner university (Toulouse 3) or designee

J. DIPLOMA HONORS (Armenian "Red Diploma"):
   For both Bachelor's (Bakalavr) and Master's (Magistros), a red diploma
   (diplôme rouge / գերազանցության դիպլոմ) is awarded if the overall
   average is >= 14/20.

K. LANGUAGE OF RECORDS:
   In case of discrepancy between Armenian, English, and French versions
   of this document, the French version prevails.

L. EFFECTIVE DATE:
   This regulation applies from the 2025-2026 academic year onwards for all
   IMA students (including those re-enrolling). It annuls the 2024-2025
   version.

title: MERIT SCHOLARSHIP ALLOCATION PROCEDURE — TIE-BREAKING RULES
body:
Source: Procedure for Calculating Merit Scholarship Places
     Approved by Rector Salwa Nacouzi, April 20, 2023

This procedure defines how problematic cases are resolved when calculating
the number of merit-based scholarship (bourse au mérite / առաջադիմության
զեղչ) places allocated by UFAR. It applies when students' overall averages
(MG / ՄՈԳ) are extremely close.

RULE 1 — DIFFERENCE OF 0.01 POINTS:
  If the difference between the overall averages of two students in the same
  faculty and same year is 0.01 points (e.g., 15.75 vs 15.74), the calculation
  is made in favor of the student.

  Example: Student A has MG = 15.748, Student B has MG = 15.744. The difference
  is 0.004. This means both students must receive an equal scholarship place
  (ex aequo / հավասար զեղչ).

RULE 2 — 25% SCHOLARSHIP CASES:
  In cases covered by Rule 1 where the student(s) with the slightly lower
  average claim a 25% scholarship, the number of scholarship places provided
  by the "Merit Scholarship Calculation Table" is INCREASED accordingly.

RULE 3 — HIGHER SCHOLARSHIP (>25%) CASES:
  In cases covered by Rule 1 where the student(s) with the slightly lower
  average claim a scholarship higher than 25% (e.g., 50%, 75%, or 100%),
  the total number of scholarship places is NOT increased.
  Instead, the number of students receiving higher scholarships is increased
  at the expense of the number of students receiving lower scholarships.

RULE 4 — NO CHAIN EFFECT:
  This decision cannot be applied as a chain process.
  If a student qualifies and receives a scholarship (or an additional
  scholarship) as a result of this procedure, then a student with an average
  lower by 0.01 points CANNOT claim the privilege defined by this decision.

EFFECTIVE DATE: April 20, 2023 (date of Rector's approval)

title: INTERNAL REGULATIONS (RÈGLEMENT INTÉRIEUR) — 2025-2026
body:
Validated by UFAR Board of Trustees, July 30, 2025
     Effective from 2025-2026 academic year
     Replaces the July 9, 2024 version
     Applies to all UFAR students regardless of location

A. STUDENT RIGHTS (Article 1.1)

1.1.1 Right of Expression:
   - Guaranteed except for injurious or defamatory writings that harm persons,
     public order, or the proper functioning of the University.
   - Only persons mandated by the Rector may make official statements on
     behalf of UFAR on social media.

1.1.2 Right of Association:
   - Any student may create an association within the university framework
     after receiving authorization from the Rector.
   - Any student is free to join existing UFAR associations, particularly
     the Student Council.

1.1.3 Right of Assembly:
   - Students are free to meet on university premises outside class hours
     in a room designated for this purpose by the Director of Studies.
   - Meetings that promote or encourage political or religious propaganda
     are strictly prohibited.

1.1.4 Right of Representation in Internal Bodies:
   Students are represented by elected student delegates in:
     - Scientific and Pedagogical Council (CSP)
     - University Disciplinary Commission
     - Improvement Council (Conseil de perfectionnement)
     - University Council (Conseil de l'Université)

B. STUDENT OBLIGATIONS (Article 1.2)

1.2.1 Punctuality and Attendance:
   - If a student is late and the class has already started, the teacher may
     refuse to admit the student and mark them absent.
   - For repeated and unjustified absences, sanctions apply per this regulation.
   - Any illness-related absence may be subject to a counter-visit by the UFAR
     doctor. The document prepared by the University doctor will be placed in
     the student's file.
   - A student may obtain an attendance dispensation from the Director of
     Studies for the duration of an event (competition, conference) recognized
     or encouraged by UFAR. Requests must be submitted one week in advance.

1.2.2 Duty of Respect and Tolerance:
   - All relations within the University (between students and/or between
     students and staff) are based on politeness, tolerance, and respect for others.
   - Communication between teachers, students, and other UFAR staff is subject
     to ethical norms. The following are PROHIBITED:
     - Calls to personal phones of UFAR employees, teachers, and administrative
       staff except by mutual agreement.
     - Requests for information outside the authority of the teacher/staff member.
     - Sending requests contrary to UFAR's regulatory documents.
     - Requests and exchanges concerning UFAR's teaching process via social
       networks or non-University email accounts, except by mutual agreement.
     - Any personal exchange (written, oral, electronic) that is offensive,
       threatening, slanderous, or blackmailing.
     - Any exchange humiliating or negative toward a person, their work,
       or their behavior.
     - Parental intervention in resolving problems concerning a student
       who is of legal age.
   - Physical, psychological, or verbal violence will result in disciplinary
     sanctions. The University reserves the right to immediately report incidents
     to competent authorities.
   - Any form of discrimination (racial, sexual, religious, or other) is
     strictly prohibited.
   - Students must always have their student ID card. Failure to present it
     may result in denial of access to the building. Lost/stolen card replacement:
     3,000 AMD. Card must be returned upon withdrawal or expulsion.
   - Guards and exam invigilators act according to University directives.
   - PROHIBITED: Using or disclosing personal or family secrets (per RA
     legislation) about another student, UFAR staff (including teachers,
     chair holders, deans, the Rector, service providers, and their family
     members) without prior consent. This includes social media (Facebook,
     Instagram, X, etc.) and apps (Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, etc.).
   - PROHIBITED: Unauthorized access to mobile devices, computers, computer
     systems, or networks belonging to other students, UFAR employees,
     or their family members.
   - PROHIBITED: Actions to destroy, modify, damage, corrupt, block, or copy
     computer data created or used by others.

1.2.3 Dress Code and Behavior:
   - Students' clothing must be clean, neat, and decent at all times.
   - Mobile phones must be on silent mode during class. They may be used only
     at the express request of the teacher. The teacher may prohibit phone use
     and give a warning for repeat offenses.
   - Strictly PROHIBITED:
     a) Bringing dangerous objects (firearms, bladed weapons, tear gas, etc.)
        into the University.
     b) Use or possession of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances
        on campus.
     c) Bringing or consuming alcoholic beverages on campus, except for
        events exceptionally authorized by the University Direction.
     d) Presence of bodyguards within the University.
     e) Card games involving money and other gambling.

1.2.4 Respect for Premises and Equipment:
   - Smoking inside buildings or sitting on window ledges is strictly prohibited.
   - Any intentional damage requires the student to pay for repair or replacement.
   - Students must maintain cleanliness of spaces.
   - Parking at the rear of the UFAR building is reserved for teaching and
     administrative staff. Students may not park there.

1.2.5 Library:
   - Governed by its own regulations (access hours, borrowing rules).
   - A place for individual study: calm and silence required.
   - Mobile phones on silent; phone conversations and discussions prohibited.
   - Librarians may expel students who do not comply after oral warning.
   - Non-return or deterioration of a book requires payment for replacement.
   - Repeat offenses may lead to sanctions.

1.2.6 Computer Rooms:
   - Governed by their own regulations (access hours, computer and program
     use rules, email and internet use rules).
   - IT staff may expel students who do not comply after oral warning.
   - Damage to equipment requires payment for repair or replacement.

1.2.7 Sports Hall:
   - Governed by its own regulations (access conditions, equipment use rules,
     safety instructions). Applies to all users: students, teaching and
     administrative staff.
   - Decent and appropriate sportswear required for Physical Education and
     Sports (EPS) classes.
   - EPS teachers may expel students who do not comply after oral warning.

C. FINANCIAL AID (Part Two) — Additional details

2.1 Academic and Social Scholarships:
   - Consist of partial or total exemption from tuition fees.
   - Represent at least 7% of total tuition fees and concern at least 10%
     of enrolled students.
   - Foreign students admitted under quotas and/or having passed a simplified
     Armenian exam may benefit from academic scholarships only from the second
     year onward.
   - Only students who have not received a disciplinary sanction equal to or
     greater than a reprimand (blâme) may apply for a scholarship. The sanction
     is lifted after two (2) semesters following the semester in which the
     sanctioned behavior occurred.
   - Only students in Years 2, 3, 4 of Bachelor's and 2nd year of Master's who
     have participated in all exams of the first session and meet other
     conditions may apply for a scholarship.

2.2 Attribution of Academic Scholarships:
   - Reviewed each academic year after first-session juries, according to
     annual overall average and amounts/distribution decided annually by the
     Board of Trustees.

2.3 Attribution of Social Scholarships (Need-Based):
   - Granted per academic year. Students submit applications according to
     UFAR's published calendar. Late applications rejected.
   - Awarded by a commission defined by the Rector.

D. EXAMINATION REGIME (Part Three) — New details

3.1 Organization of Sessions:

3.1.1 For Bachelor's Years 3-4 and Master's students (2025-2026):
   - Two exam sessions per semester (first session and second session/retake)
     per the university calendar, except for special modalities (oral exams,
     French visiting professor exams, continuous assessment, internships).
   - If a course ends before the session start, the exam may be organized
     7 days after the last class.

3.1.2 Redoubling (Course Repetition):
   - Students repeating a year must follow French and English classes.
   - They do not need to retake French/English exams if they already have
     >=10/20 and earned ECTS credits.

3.1.3 Absences (detailed rules):
   - For Years 3-4 Bachelor's and Master's: Absence from first session does
     not prevent participation in second session. Absent from both sessions = 0.
   - For Years 1-2 Bachelor's: Absence from E1 and E2 requires justification
     to Director of Studies. Make-up sessions: E1 in November, E2 in
     December-January for first semester; mid-semester 2 and end of semester 2
     for second semester. Make-ups possible ONLY for force majeure (e.g.,
     hospitalization). If absence unjustified = 0.

3.2 Conditions for Exam Participation:

3.2.1 Seating:
   - Students must sit in assigned seats. Otherwise, exam paper is annulled.
   - Student ID card must be presented at the start and placed on the table
     corner for the entire exam. If forgotten, passport or national ID may be
     accepted exceptionally.

3.2.2 Lateness:
   - 15 minutes after the scheduled start, student is no longer admitted
     regardless of reason.
   - If admitted within 15 minutes, the student may write only until the
     originally scheduled end time.
   - If during those 15 minutes other students completed a listening exercise,
     the late student automatically loses the opportunity to complete it.

3.2.3 Prohibited Materials:
   - Mobile phone, smartwatch, or any other communicating electronic device
     (even turned off) is prohibited.
   - Use of any document is prohibited except as per 3.2.4.
   - Possession of prohibited documents or electronic devices, even without
     use, constitutes fraud and will be sanctioned by the Disciplinary
     Commission.
   - The University reserves the right to detect electronic equipment during
     exams by various means.

3.2.4 Authorized Materials:
   - Only blue ink pens are allowed.
   - Calculators and reference documents are allowed only if indicated on
     the exam subject. They cannot be shared between students.
   - If the teacher authorizes reference documents, they must inform the
     Director of Studies in writing, specifying document names and whether
     students bring them or they are distributed by invigilators.

3.2.5 Exam Conduct:
   - Students receive one blank exam booklet and numbered scratch paper from
     the University. Any additional booklet must be noted by the invigilator.
   - If the subject requires answers written on it, it is stapled to the booklet.
   - Strictly prohibited to communicate with other students during the exam.
   - Leaving the exam room for any reason is prohibited. Any exit is final
     and can only occur 30 minutes after the start, except to go to the
     medical officer's office accompanied by an invigilator or doctor.

3.2.6 Incidents:
   - Students must inform invigilators of any error, incident, or suspected
     error in the exam subject.
   - If an error is confirmed, the University may cancel the exam and reschedule it.

3.2.7 End of Exam:
   - Students return exam booklets to invigilators and sign the attendance
     list before leaving.
   - Scratch paper and subject are returned separately.
   - Invigilators mark the last page and blank pages with a red "Z".
   - Invigilators prepare a report with: number of registered students,
     number present, number absent, number of copies collected, observations
     and incidents.
   - Copies and report are sealed, collected by the Academic Office, then
     given to teachers who sign a register.

3.3 Exam Supervision:

3.3.1 Invigilators:
   - The University may call upon external staff. A register of invigilators
     is created. Organization is the responsibility of the Director of Studies.

3.3.2 Exam Room Surveillance:
   - Each room is monitored by at least one invigilator.
   - The exam room may be placed under video surveillance as well as
     electronic communication jamming devices. The IT department is responsible
     for recording and archiving video data.

3.3.3 Role of Invigilator in Case of Fraud or Attempted Fraud:
   - The invigilator must seize all documents or materials, prepare a detailed
     report (including exact time), countersigned by the invigilator and the
     student(s). The student may write their version of facts in the report.
   - If the student refuses to countersign, the invigilator notes this in writing.
   - In case of person substitution or disturbances, expulsion from the exam
     room may be considered.
   - If the student is not expelled, their copy is treated like others, but
     no grade report is issued before the Disciplinary Commission's decision.
   - Copies written with a pen other than blue, or bearing ostensible signs
     (images, symbols, letters, numbers unrelated to exam content in margins),
     will NOT be corrected or graded.
   - Any exam paper must begin on page 1. Papers starting on page 2 will be
     considered as bearing a distinctive sign and will NOT be corrected.

3.4 Fraud (Article 3.4):

3.4.1 Plagiarism:
   - Reproducing any text, part of a text, literary or graphic material,
     or reformulating any text without citing the author.
   - Self-plagiarism (reproducing one's own work without citing the source)
     is also plagiarism.
   - Plagiarism is a violation of academic ethics and, when detected in
     evaluated work, constitutes fraud. It is theft of intellectual property.
   - The University uses plagiarism detection software.
   - The sanction from the Disciplinary Commission must correspond to the
     seriousness of the plagiarism.

3.4.2 Exam Fraud includes:
   - Speaking with other students during exams/evaluations.
   - Using unauthorized documents or information.
   - Possession of unauthorized documents, especially cheat sheets,
     electronic devices (even turned off): mobile phones, smartwatches, etc.
   - Identity falsification during exams/evaluations.
   - Plagiarism.
   - Others.

3.5 Exam Subjects (Article 3.5):

3.5.1 General Framework (Years 3-4 Bachelor's and Master's):
   - Exam subjects must be transmitted to the Director of Studies at least
     15 days before the exam date.
   - If two answers to the same question coexist on one copy without clear
     indication of which version the student chooses, the question is not evaluated.

3.5.2 Special Cases: Exams Requiring Random Drawing of Subjects:
   - Semi-annual exams requiring random drawing are organized from lists of
     questions and exercises previously transmitted to the Director of Studies
     and validated by deans and chair holders.
   - Organization of the draw is the responsibility of the Director of Studies.

E. GRADES (Part Four)

4.1 Consultation of Exam Copies:
   - Possible after grades are posted, in the presence of the teacher.
   - The faculty responsible sets the consultation date within one week after
     the teacher returns copies, but no later than 3 days before the semester jury.
   - Students absent lose the opportunity to consult their work.
   - Students may only bring their student ID. They may not consult another
     student's copy. Photographing copies is prohibited.
   - Grades become final only after jury deliberation and official posting.
   - Students may check for technical errors (calculation or transcription
     errors) but cannot request a second correction of their copy.
   - For technical errors, students submit a written appeal to their faculty
     responsible (room 107) specifying the teacher's name, subject, and
     identification details. Appeal must be submitted on the consultation day
     or the following working day, but no later than the day before the jury.
   - Any grade change due to calculation or data entry error must be validated
     by the Director of Studies. This must be done within 3 working days of
     receiving the written appeal, but no later than the day before the jury.

4.2 Grade Evaluation Commission:
   - May be convened to harmonize Armenian and French grading approaches and
     discuss issues related to exam, internship report, and thesis grades.
   - Composition: Rector (President), Vice-Rector for Education/Research/
     University Life, Director of Studies, deans of UFAR and partner university
     faculties.
   - Decisions are final. If cheating is suspected, the file is transmitted
     to the Disciplinary Commission.

F. SANCTIONS (Part Five)

5.1 General Framework:
   - For each violation of these Internal Regulations or other UFAR regulations,
     an appropriate sanction applies: oral reminder, temporary exclusion from
     class or service, or for serious or repeat offenses: warning, reprimand
     (blâme), prohibition of free or subsidized places, prohibition of exam,
     expulsion.
   - Sanctions are imposed by the Rector after convening the Disciplinary Commission.

5.2 Disciplinary Commission:

5.2.1 Function: Application of sanctions provided for in the Internal Regulations.

5.2.2 Composition:
   - Rector (President)
   - Director of Studies
   - Vice-Rector for Education, Research, and University Life
   - Dean or Chair Holder concerned (or designee)
   - A representative of the Academic Office
   - President of the Student Council (or representative)
   - Assistant to the Director of Studies (minutes)
   - Head of the Rector's Cabinet
   - Associate Dean of the French partner university (if the alleged facts
     occurred during evaluation of a course taught by a teacher from that
     partner university; may participate by videoconference)

5.2.3 Organization:
   - Convened at the request of the President or on proposal of the Director
     of Studies to the Rector.
   - Suspected students must be present and may be represented or assisted
     by a person of their choice. If unjustifiably absent, the session may
     proceed.

5.2.4 Decisions:
   - Decisions made by majority of members present. Rector's casting vote
     in case of tie.

5.3 Applicable Sanctions:

   Principal Sanctions:
     - Oral warning
     - Written warning
     - Reprimand (blâme)
     - Reprimand resulting in a zero on the exam
     - Other sanctions depending on number and complexity of cases
     - Exclusion from the institution for a period set by the Commission

   Secondary Sanctions:
     - Prohibition or loss of academic scholarships for a period set by the
       Disciplinary Commission
     - Prohibition or loss of need-based scholarships (social criteria) for
       a period set by the Disciplinary Commission
     - Loss of eligibility for an internship abroad

   Principal and/or secondary sanctions may be suspended (with probation).

5.4 Absences (Article 5.4) — reiterates existing policy from Section 22A:
   - Justified absences: medical certificate or civil status document; written
     notification to Director of Studies within 2 days; document to Academic
     Office within 8 days.
   - 30 unexcused absences: loss of scholarship for current year and/or ban
     from academic scholarships for a period set by Disciplinary Commission.
   - 50 unexcused absences: exclusion from the institution.

5.5 Cumulative Sanctions and Serious Cases:
   - Repeat offenses may result in severer sanctions.
   - For any question not specifically governed by this regulation, the Rector
     may issue a decision.
   - In case of force majeure, the regulation may be modified by order of
     the Rector.

G. GENERAL PROVISIONS

   - A student is administratively enrolled once they have signed their contract
     and paid the tuition fees in force.
   - This regulation replaces and annuls the Internal Regulation adopted by
     the Board of Trustees on July 9, 2024.
   - In case of force majeure, the regulation may be modified by order of
     the Rector.
